claim: Dokku is a Docker-powered PaaS with 31.9k GitHub stars; v0.38.17 released June 3, 2026; MIT license; written in Shell (54%) and Go (42%)
quote: A docker-powered PaaS that helps you build and manage the lifecycle of applications

claim: Dokku is an open-source PaaS alternative to Heroku, extensible via plugins in any language, no vendor lock-in
quote: An open source PAAS alternative to Heroku

claim: Dokku supports Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 and Debian 11+ on AMD64 and arm64; minimum 1 GB RAM (or swap)
quote: 1GB of system memory, or add swap memory

claim: Core workflow: create app, add git remote, git push dokku main; apps must honour PORT env var; apps auto-created on first push
quote: the remote username must be dokku or pushes will fail

claim: Dokku idles at ~95 MB RAM with ~15 s boot time; Coolify idles at 380 MB with 45 s boot; resource metrics from live testing
quote: Platform RAM (idle): Coolify 380MB, CapRover 210MB, Dokku 95MB; Boot time: ~15s

claim: Dokku is single-server only with no RBAC, no multi-user support, and varying plugin quality across the community ecosystem
quote: Dokku is single-server only with no built-in way to deploy to multiple servers or do horizontal scaling across machines

claim: Official Let's Encrypt plugin with 1.1k stars; auto-renewal via daily cron; supports HTTP-01 and DNS-01 challenges
quote: schedules daily auto-renewals, so existing certificates renew themselves before they expire

claim: GitHub Action for Dokku PR preview deployments; creates per-PR apps on PR open, destroys on close; concurrent pushes cause deploy-lock failures
quote: Pushing changes too rapidly causes failures due to deploy locks

claim: More complete PR preview scaffold with auto-SSL, multi-database support, Trivy scanning, and cleanup on PR close; requires 4+ GB RAM
quote: every PR getting its own live URL, automatic SSL with Let's Encrypt certificates, and automatic cleanup of orphaned apps

claim: Official plugins cover PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, Meilisearch, Let's Encrypt, Grafana, Kubernetes/Nomad schedulers
quote: Community plugins may not have been tested by Dokku maintainers

claim: Builder auto-detection: project.toml triggers pack-cli (CNB), Dockerfile triggers docker build, else falls back to Herokuish buildpacks
quote: Dokku normally defaults to using Heroku buildpacks for deployment, though this may be overridden by committing a valid Dockerfile

claim: Dokku gives full server control and cost savings vs managed PaaS; requires server management knowledge; git-push is the entire deployment workflow
quote: Install it on a fresh Ubuntu server, add a git remote, and git push dokku main is the entire workflow
